content.comment_body: I find using the cursor keys convenient for adjusting parameters, but it's frustrating that you must always hold the ESC button at the same time. I read that [company_name] changed this issue with the introduction of the [product_name] display, but after trying it myself, that doesn’t seem to be true. Is there a way to use the cursor keys alone for interacting with the program, without needing the ESC button? Thanks in advance... [user_name]

As I expected. My last option is to disconnect and physically remove the [product_name] cursor buttons, then replace them with pushbuttons wired to the digital inputs. Fortunately, there are some spare connections on the [product_name] module. Regards, [user_name]
Does that mean you've already tried all the F keys and their combinations?

Yes, I have. Even if the function buttons weren’t already assigned, I’d still like to use the four cursor keys more easily. I understand why two-handed operation exists, but a more user-friendly HMI would let you disable this feature, even if it means some functions can’t be changed directly from the display. That’s just my perspective.

I hope [company_name] gives us the option to disable the ESC function on the [product_name] display. It would be very useful for many users! I’ve had similar issues and my solution was to create different text message operation panels for moving three axes on drilling machines: one for turret Z, one for travel X, and one for travel Y. I used three digital inputs to select among the three blocks, which required fewer digital inputs overall.

analysis.insight_summary: Users consistently experience frustration with having to press the ESC button when using cursor keys on the [product_name] display, particularly for parameter changes and repeated actions. This limitation disrupts workflow efficiency and leads some to look for hardware modifications or design custom solutions to make the interface easier to use.
analysis.user_expectations: Users would like the ability to operate cursor keys independently, without requiring the ESC button for every adjustment. This change would allow for a smoother, simpler HMI experience and reduce repetitive strain during parameter setting.
